# Medical Handbook
## Order of care
1. Select a body zone on the targeting doll. 2. Stop external bleeding. 3. Check oxygenation, circulating blood, perfusion, and heart rhythm. 4. Perform a handheld analysis or a full body scan. 5. Stabilize breathing and circulation. 6. Treat wounds and immobilize fractures. 7. Perform the required surgical intervention. 8. Repeat diagnostics.
## Core equipment
- [color=#58e6d9]HandheldHealthAnalyzer[/color] — approximate vital signs and visible external injuries. - [color=#58e6d9]MedicalScanner + computerBodyScanner[/color] — complete wound, organ, fracture, drug, and cyberware diagnostics. - [color=#58e6d9]Gauze[/color] — dressing for external capillary and venous bleeding. - [color=#58e6d9]Brutepack[/color] — hemostatic packing for a deep external wound. - [color=#58e6d9]Tourniquet[/color] — control of external bleeding from a limb. - [color=#58e6d9]NCFieldSplint[/color] — temporary stabilization of a limb fracture. - [color=#58e6d9]NCManualVentilator[/color] — temporary assisted ventilation. - [color=#58e6d9]Bloodpack[/color] — restores blood in the bloodstream solution. - [color=#58e6d9]Defibrillator[/color] — treats a shockable cardiac arrest rhythm.
